question: Choose the visual world for the Bible Read design rehaul:

options.label: The Sanctuary Liturgy & Canonical Hours
options.thesis: Daily reading mapped to the gentle rhythm of canonical light, where presence in scripture is marked with warm beeswax gold and calm stone stillness.
options.viewport: A calm mobile screen anchored by the day's ambient sky banner (shifting dawn to night), a prominent 'Today's Reading' card with serif scripture headlines, and a subtle gold thread connecting the reader to their Circle.
options.risk: Requires careful contrast tuning so ambient sky tones never reduce reading legibility.

raised.raise: Bible book coverage and testament laps visualized as illuminated magnitude rings rather than generic progress bars.
A circular letterpressed seal for milestone Badges and read-through celebrations.

options.label: The Rubricated Daily Office
options.lineage: 1662 Book of Common Prayer & liturgical lectionaries
options.thesis: The timeless dignity of a personal prayer book: deep iron-gall ink, warm linen paper, and rubricated crimson markers for daily passages.
options.viewport: Generous editorial margins with rubricated chapter numbers in red, warm linen cards, and an understated daily check-in ribbon.
options.risk: Also the direction most runs in this category land on; can feel overly traditional if UI typography isn't razor-sharp.

options.label: The Celestial Nocturne
options.thesis: Scripture reading as navigating the heavens: deep midnight indigo, star-magnitude chapter dots, and night-vision amber accents.
options.viewport: A deep dark-mode mobile screen where Bible coverage glows like constellations and daily check-in illuminates today's coordinate.
options.case: Fuses beautifully with testament lap tracking and night-time reflection; brings cosmic wonder to habit tracking.
options.risk: Leans heavily into dark mode; daytime reading requires an equally refined light-chart counterpart.

options.label: The Design Annual Plate Section
options.case: Loses on audience identification: readers want devotional warmth, not an exhibition catalog.
options.kept: Circular letterpressed seal for milestone Badges.

options.label: Datamatics Sine Lattice
options.case: Loses on both axes: stroboscopic B&W frequency bands clash completely with contemplative Scripture.
options.kept: Tabular schedule discipline and monospace verse metrics.

canonCard.label: The Clean Modern Devotional
canonCard.thesis: The category standard: clean Material 3 cards, standard typography, and conventional mobile layouts.
canonCard.viewport: Standard clean mobile cards with rounded corners, bottom navigation bar, and clean sans typography.
canonCard.risk: Familiar and functional, but visually indistinct from generic habit trackers.
